Sierpinski's Gasket and Dihedral Symmetry

SequencesDivisibilityCounting
Game: Start with one coloured square in the corner and let a simple rule spread it over the grid. Watch the pattern it makes.
How to play: Press +1 to take a step, or a bigger number for several. Try Add or Replace, and 2 or 3 prongs.
Algorithm
# prongs
Look for the math

Number the rows n and the columns m from 0 at the top-left corner, which starts with a 1. At every step all cells change together:

Add, 2 prongs: S(n,m) + S(n−1,m) + S(n,m−1)
Replace, 2 prongs: S(n−1,m) + S(n,m−1)
Add, 3 prongs: S(n,m) + S(n−1,m−1) + S(n−1,m) + S(n,m−1)

and the picture colours each cell by its value modulo M. Modulo 2 the coloured cells form the Sierpinski gasket.

Replace is Pascal's triangle

With Replace each cell is the sum of the cell above and the cell to the left, the rule of Pascal's triangle, tipped on its side: cell (n, m) holds C(n+m, n) once the growing edge has passed it. On a grid of size 2p, run to the corner modulo 2, Add draws exactly the same picture; on other sizes the two are quite different. The test checked both for every size up to 64.

A symmetry that should not be there

The Add rule looks lopsided, yet at every step its triangle of colours is unchanged by the six symmetries of an equilateral triangle (once it is sheared into one). The reason is a formula: after N steps cell (n, m) holds

C(N−m, n) · C(N, m) = N! / (n! m! k!), with k = N − n − m,

a multinomial coefficient, which does not care which of n, m, k is which. With 3 prongs the cell holds C(N, n) · C(N, m), and the square picture has the eight symmetries of a square (the dihedral group).

What was checked

The logic test ran every rule on grids of 2 to 24 cells, for many moduli, step by step to the edge, and found the page's formulas exact in every cell, the triangle's six symmetries and the square's eight at every step, and Replace with 3 prongs giving the Delannoy numbers.

Set N to 27 and Modulo to 3, choose Add and run To corner. Then try N = 32 with Modulo 2 and compare Add and Replace.
